elements.id-string-10: We revisit the proposal of \cite{Fiset:2021ruv} for the worldsheet description of string theory compactifications on special holonomy manifolds obtained via connected sums: the geometric construction corresponds to a diamond of inclusions of worldsheet algebras.
elements.id-string-11: We present new  evidence for the proposal by considering compactifications on the Schoen Calabi--Yau manifold.
elements.id-string-13: The purpose of this note is to provide further evidence in favour of a proposal of \cite{Fiset:2021ruv} regarding the worldsheet formulation of string theory compactifications on connected sum manifolds.
elements.id-string-14: Connected sum manifolds are obtained by gluing two Asymptotically Cylindrical (ACyl) open manifolds along isomorphic asymptotic ends.
elements.id-string-15: This technique has proved extremely fruitful to construct compact manifolds of special holonomy \cite{Kovalev:2003, Corti:2012, Corti:2012kd, Crowley:2015ctv, Nordstrom:2018cli, Goette:2020, Braun:2018joh} which have then been used to study string compactifications, see for example \cite{Halverson:2014tya, Braun:2017ryx, Braun:2017uku, Braun:2018vhk, Heckman:2018mxl} and references therein.
elements.id-string-16: From the point of view of the worldsheet, a string theory compactification on a special holonomy manifold corresponds to an extended algebra of chiral symmetries \cite{Odake:1988bh, Shatashvili:1994zw, Figueroa-OFarrill:1996tnk}.
elements.id-string-17: This can be understood from the fact that covariantly constant forms give rise to new worldsheet symmetries and their associated currents \cite{Howe:1991vs, Howe:1991im,  Howe:1991ic}.
elements.id-string-18: This correspondence is further enhanced when the compactifying manifold can be described in terms of a connected sum.
elements.id-string-19: The features of this geometric structure are reflected in the worldsheet in terms of a diamond of inclusions of chiral algebras \cite{Fiset:2021ruv}.
elements.id-string-20: This has been verified for Twisted Connected Sum (TCS) \cite{Fiset:2018huv}, Extra Twisted Connected Sum (ETCS) and Generalized Connected Sum (GCS) manifolds \cite{Fiset:2021ruv}.
elements.id-string-21: In this note we check that this proposal also holds for the Schoen Calabi--Yau manifold \cite{Schoen1988}.
elements.id-string-22: The connected sum structure of this manifold was obtained in \cite{Braun:2017uku} by applying M-theory/heterotic duality to TCS G$_2$-manifold compactifications.
elements.id-string-23: Consequently, we will find that the associated diamond of algebras presents some similarities with that of the TCS.
elements.id-string-24: This note is organised as follows: we first introduce in \cref{sec:Background} some necessary background on connected sums and worldsheet algebras together with a summary of the proposal of \cite{Fiset:2021ruv}.
elements.id-string-25: In \cref{sec:TCS} we discuss as a warm-up case---and with the purpose of setting up notation---the example of TCS G$_2$-manifolds.
elements.id-string-26: This case was already analysed in \cite{Fiset:2018huv}, but here we have modified the presentation to follow \cite{Fiset:2021ruv}.
elements.id-string-27: \Cref{sec:Schoen} contains the most important results of this note.
elements.id-string-28: We begin with a review of the connected sum structure of the Schoen manifold following \cite{Braun:2017uku} before introducing the corresponding diamond of chiral algebras.
elements.id-string-29: We proceed to study the diamond in detail, looking at the the relationship between the algebra at the bottom and the intersection of the algebras at the lateral tips.
elements.id-string-30: We then study automorphisms of the diamond and relate them to mirror symmetry maps, before summarizing our results and concluding in \cref{sec:Conclusion}.
elements.id-string-32: Special holonomy manifolds via connected sums
elements.id-string-33: The Twisted Connected Sum (TCS) construction was introduced by Kovalev \cite{Kovalev:2003} and later extended by Corti, Haskins, Nordstr\"om and Pacini \cite{Corti:2012, Corti:2012kd} to provide new examples of compact manifolds with G$_2$-holonomy.
elements.id-string-34: This technique has been further generalized within the G$_2$-holonomy setting to the Extra Twisted Connected Sum (ETCS) construction \cite{Crowley:2015ctv, Nordstrom:2018cli, Goette:2020}, and several alternative versions of these ``connected sum'' constructions have been proposed with the aim of producing new manifolds with holonomy $\text{SU}(3)$ \cite{Doi:2013}, $\text{SU}(4)$ \cite{Doi:2015} or $\text{Spin}(7)$ \cite{Braun:2018joh, Doi:2019}.\footnote{The Generalized Connected Sum (GCS) of Spin(7)-holonomy manifolds proposed in \cite{Braun:2018joh} is supported by strong evidence from string theory compactifications \cite{Braun:2018joh, Cvetic:2020piw, Fiset:2021ruv}.
elements.id-string-35: Nevertheless, a formal mathematical proof of its general validity is still missing in the literature.}
elements.id-string-36: We now describe the general ideas underlying all these constructions, and refer the reader to the original papers as well as \cite{Langlais:2023pmo} for the technical details.

elements.id-string-47: We want to obtain a compact manifold $M$ with holonomy equal to $G$.
elements.id-string-48: To this end, we consider two ACyl manifolds $M_\pm$ with cross-sections $N_\pm\,$.
elements.id-string-49: Both $M_\pm$ must have holonomy contained in $G$, so they are both equipped with torsion-free $G$-structures.
elements.id-string-50: We also require the cross-sections $N_\pm$ to be isomorphic.
elements.id-string-51: We call these ACyl manifolds the \emph{building blocks} of the construction.
elements.id-string-52: The next step is to glue the two building blocks along their isomorphic asymptotic ends to produce a compact manifold $M$.
elements.id-string-53: Parametrizing the directions of the cylinders $\R^+_\pm$ by $t_\pm\,$, we truncate both cylinders and introduce boundaries at $t_\pm=t_0+1$.
elements.id-string-54: We can then define an isomorphism $F_{t_0}$ between $\left[ t_0,t_0+1 \right]_+\times N_+$ and $\left[ t_0,t_0+1 \right]_-\times N_-$ as follows
elements.id-string-55: \begin{equation} F_{t_0}:\left[ t_0,t_0+1 \right]_+\times N_+ \ni \left(t,n\right) \longmapsto \left(2 t_0+1-t,\phi(n)\right) \in \left[ t_0,t_0+1 \right]_-\times N_- \, , \end{equation}
elements.id-string-56: where $\phi$ is an isomorphism between $N_+$ and $N_-\,$.
elements.id-string-57: We call $F_{t_0}$ the \emph{gluing map}, it identifies the asymptotic ends of $M_\pm$ and produces a compact manifold $M$.
elements.id-string-58: The area where the gluing is performed is usually denominated the \emph{neck} region of $M$, and we will denote it by $M_+\cap M_-\,$.
elements.id-string-59: The gluing map is chosen such that the $G$-structures of $M_\pm$ can be patched together into a globally well-defined $G$-structure on $M$.
elements.id-string-60: As we have truncated $M_\pm$ at $t_\pm=t_0+1$, the $G$-structure on $M$ has non-trivial torsion localized in the neck region.
elements.id-string-61: The key point of the construction is that through some careful analysis it can be shown that for a sufficiently long neck---equivalently, for large enough $t_0$---it is possible to deform the $G$-structure to a torsion-free one.

elements.id-string-64: Worldsheet algebras for special holonomy manifolds
elements.id-string-65: We now focus on worldsheet aspects of string theory compactifications on special holonomy manifolds.
elements.id-string-66: For the purpose of this note, we will consider supersymmetric type II backgrounds given by a direct product of a special holonomy manifold $M$ and Minkowski spacetime.
elements.id-string-67: In practice, we will ignore the spacetime factor and study these compactifications in terms of an $\mathcal{N}=(1,1)$ non-linear sigma model with target $M$.
elements.id-string-68: From the worldsheet point of view, this is described by a two-dimensional chiral superconformal field theory.
elements.id-string-69: Throughout this note we restrict ourselves to one of the chiral components, say the holomorphic one, and study the underlying superconformal algebra.
elements.id-string-70: The special holonomy of the target manifold $M$ has important consequences for the sigma model.
elements.id-string-71: Recall that reduced holonomy can be equivalently formulated as the existence of certain covariantly constant forms on the manifold \cite{Joyce:2007}.
elements.id-string-72: It was observed by Howe and Papadopoulos \cite{Howe:1991vs, Howe:1991im,  Howe:1991ic} that each of these covariantly constant forms leads to an additional (classical) non-linear chiral symmetry on the sigma model action.
elements.id-string-73: The conserved (super-)currents associated to these symmetries are constructed directly from the covariantly constant forms.
elements.id-string-74: At the level of the quantum worldsheet theory, this implies the existence of additional chiral operators corresponding to the covariantly constant forms on $M$.
elements.id-string-75: These operators come in supersymmetric pairs: to each $p$-form we can associate an operator of conformal weight $\frac{p}{2}$ and its supersymmetric partner of weight $\frac{p+1}{2}\,$.
elements.id-string-76: Furthermore, these operators retain some features reminiscent of their geometric origin, as we will motivate in more detail in an example below.
elements.id-string-77: We thus find that the original underlying $\mathcal{N}=1$ (super-)Virasoro algebra, given by the (holomorphic) stress-tensor $T$ and the chiral supersymmetry current $G$, can be extended by additional operators to obtain a new $\mathcal{N}=1$ W-algebra \cite{Odake:1988bh, Shatashvili:1994zw, Figueroa-OFarrill:1990tqt, Figueroa-OFarrill:1990mzn, Blumenhagen:1991nm, Figueroa-OFarrill:1996tnk}.
elements.id-string-78: This means that we can associate to each special holonomy manifold $M$ a particular chiral algebra $\mathcal{A}(M)$ that captures the underlying chiral symmetries upon compactification.
elements.id-string-79: We illustrate this with an example: consider a K\"ahler $n$-fold, that is, a $2n$-dimensional manifold with $\text{U}(n)$-holonomy.
elements.id-string-80: This manifold comes equipped with a covariantly constant Hermitian 2-form $\omega_n\,$, which gives rise to a weight $1$ superprimary multiplet $(J^3_n,G^3_n)$.
elements.id-string-81: This extends the original $\mathcal{N}=1$ Virasoro algebra to an $\mathcal{N}=2$ Virasoro algebra and reflects the fact that a compactification on a K\"ahler manifold preserves $\mathcal{N}=2$ supersymmetry.
elements.id-string-82: The most relevant case for us will be when the holonomy is further reduced to $\text{SU}(n)$, which corresponds to a Calabi--Yau $n$-fold.
elements.id-string-83: In this situation we have an additional covariantly constant complex $n$-form known as the holomorphic volume form $\Omega_n\,$.
elements.id-string-84: This results in two additional real superprimary multiplets of conformal weight $\frac{n}{2}$ corresponding to the real and imaginary part of $\Omega_n\,$.
elements.id-string-87: These further extend the $\mathcal{N}=2$ Virasoro algebra of the K\"ahler case to the \emph{Odake algebra} \cite{Odake:1988bh}, which we denote by $\text{Od}_n \,$.
elements.id-string-88: For $n\geq 3$ the Odake algebra is associative modulo the following \emph{singular} fields and their descendants (which we call \emph{null} fields)
elements.id-string-89: \begin{equation}  N^1_n = \partial A_n \; -\normord{J^3_n\, B_n} \, , \qquad N^2_n = \partial B_n \; +\normord{J^3_n\, A_n} \, , \end{equation}
elements.id-string-91: Singular fields are descendants which are annihilated by all positive modes of the generators of the algebra.
elements.id-string-92: They have zero norm, so they do not contribute to correlation functions and they must be quotiented out of our extended algebras.
elements.id-string-93: This is a subtle point in the analysis of this note, as many of the statements we check are true ``up to null fields''.
elements.id-string-94: The case $n=2$ of the Odake algebra is very special as it corresponds to K3 surfaces, which are also hyper-K\"ahler manifolds.

elements.id-string-101: Another example of the correlation between geometry and algebra can be seen as follows: the $\text{Od}_2$ algebra is actually isomorphic to the (little) $\mathcal{N}=4$ Virasoro algebra, obtained by extending $\mathcal{N}=1$ Virasoro by an $\text{SU}(2)$ Kac--Moody current super-algebra at level $k=1$.

elements.id-string-103: We conclude this section mentioning some additional W-algebras that will be relevant for the discussion.
elements.id-string-104: The extended algebras associated to manifolds of holonomy G$_2$ and Spin(7) were introduced by Shatashvili and Vafa \cite{Shatashvili:1994zw}.
elements.id-string-105: We call these the Shatashvili--Vafa G$_2$ and Spin(7) algebras, and denote them by $\SVseven$ and $\SVeight$ respectively.

elements.id-string-115: Worldsheet algebras for connected sum manifolds
elements.id-string-116: When the manifold $M$ has a connected sum structure, the correspondence between the holonomy of $M$ and its associated W-algebra---which we denote by $\mathcal{A}(M)$---can be further extended.
elements.id-string-117: It has been proposed \cite{Fiset:2018huv, Fiset:2021ruv} that the piecewise decomposition of $M$ has its counterpart at the level of worldsheet superconformal algebras, so that chiral algebras can be associated to the building blocks $M_\pm$ as well as the neck region $M_+\cap M_-$ and arranged into a diamond of inclusions that matches the embeddings in geometry.
elements.id-string-118: The argument for the proposal goes as follows: we consider an open submanifold $U$ of the manifold $M$ and study the algebra $\mathcal{A}(U)$ of chiral operators associated to $U$.
elements.id-string-119: The covariantly constant forms on $M$ restrict to covariantly constant forms on $U$, so the corresponding operators also belong to $\mathcal{A}(U)$.
elements.id-string-120: Nevertheless, there can be covariantly constant forms on $U$ which are not well-defined over the whole of $M$.
elements.id-string-121: Equivalently, the holonomy of $U$ might be further reduced than the holonomy of $M$.
elements.id-string-122: This means the chiral algebras and the corresponding submanifolds follow the opposite inclusion pattern
elements.id-string-124: We point out that the algebra inclusion in \eqref{eq:subalgebraembedding} might not be unique, reflecting the additional geometric freedom available in the submanifold $U$.
elements.id-string-125: Consider now a different open submanifold $V\subset M$, which again satisfies $\mathcal{A}(V)\supset \mathcal{A}(M)$, and the overlap of the two open patches $U\cap V$.
elements.id-string-126: Following the reasoning of \eqref{eq:subalgebraembedding}, we can find $\mathcal{A}(M)$ as a subalgebra of $\mathcal{A}(U\cap V)$ via the inclusion $\mathcal{A}(U)\subset \mathcal{A}(U\cap V)$ or the inclusion $\mathcal{A}(V)\subset \mathcal{A}(U\cap V)$.
elements.id-string-127: Since $\mathcal{A}(M)$ represents the chiral symmetries of the whole manifold, both realizations of the inclusion should agree: this restricts some of the freedom present in the embedding \eqref{eq:subalgebraembedding}.
elements.id-string-128: The same argument can be repeated with further open patches of $M$ and in the end the embedding of $\mathcal{A}(M)$ should be uniquely fixed, as there should be no ambiguity in identifying the chiral symmetries of the theory.
elements.id-string-129: Connected sum manifolds constitute a very particular case since they are completely described by just two open submanifolds---the building blocks $M_\pm$---glued along their intersection---the neck region $M_+\cap M_-\,$.
elements.id-string-130: Following the previous arguments, we should be able to arrange the chiral algebras associated to $M$, $M_\pm$ and $M_+\cap M_-$ in a diamond of inclusions uniquely determined by the geometry of the connected sum construction.
elements.id-string-132: This line of reasoning is a motivation rather than a proof, and the validity of this proposal has to be checked on a case-by-case basis.
elements.id-string-133: This has been done so far for TCS G$_2$-manifolds \cite{Fiset:2018huv}, ETCS G$_2$-manifolds and GCS Spin(7)-manifolds \cite{Fiset:2021ruv}.
elements.id-string-134: We present in \cref{sec:Schoendiamond} a new check of the proposal for the Schoen manifold.
elements.id-string-135: The gluing map of a connected sum is an isomorphism of $M_+\cap M_-$ that provides a well-defined $G$-structure on the compact manifold $M$.
elements.id-string-136: An analogous structure should also be present for the diamond and this is indeed the case: the gluing map can be translated into an automorphism of $\mathcal{A}(M_+\cap M_-)$ that preserves $\mathcal{A}(M)$.
elements.id-string-137: We now comment on the chiral algebra corresponding to the intersection of the lateral tips of the diamond $\mathcal{A}(M_+)\cap\mathcal{A}(M_-)$.
elements.id-string-138: By construction, $\mathcal{A}(M)$ is contained inside this algebra and we might wonder if this inclusion is strict.
elements.id-string-139: If that was the case, this would mean that the set of chiral symmetries of $M$ could be further enhanced beyond those associated to a generic manifold with $G$-holonomy.
elements.id-string-140: On the other hand, an agreement between these algebras would indicate that the connected sum construction considered produces---at least from a worldsheet point of view---generic manifolds of $G$-holonomy.
elements.id-string-141: An analytical proof of this equality is currently beyond reach as the vacuum characters of extended W-algebra intersections are poorly understood.
elements.id-string-142: Nevertheless, we provided in \cite{Fiset:2021ruv} numerical checks for the connected sums mentioned above up to a certain level in the vacuum modules.
elements.id-string-143: Similar checks are presented in this note for the Schoen manifold.
elements.id-string-144: Finally, we would like to point out that the diamond of algebras can be used to study mirror symmetry for connected sum manifolds $M$.
elements.id-string-145: A mirror map in geometry corresponds to a certain algebra automorphism of the associated chiral algebra $\mathcal{A}(M)$.
elements.id-string-146: However, if $M$ admits a connected sum decomposition, a mirror map respecting the connected sum structure should correspond to an automorphism of the whole diamond of inclusions.
elements.id-string-147: This was studied in \cite{Fiset:2021ruv} for GCS Spin(7)-manifolds.
elements.id-string-148: Even though the only automorphism of $\SVeight$ is the identity, it was found that non-trivial automorphisms of the whole diamond exist and these were used to propose new GCS mirror maps beyond the ones described in \cite{Braun:2019lnn}.
elements.id-string-149: The validity of these mirror maps was explicitly checked for GCS Spin(7)-manifolds given by Joyce orbifolds \cite{Joyce:1996} admitting an SYZ fibration \cite{Strominger:1996it}.
elements.id-string-151: Review of superconformal algebras for TCS G$_2$-manifolds
elements.id-string-152: In this section we briefly recall the Twisted Connected Sum construction (TCS) of G$_2$-holonomy manifolds \cite{Kovalev:2003, Corti:2012, Corti:2012kd} and the corresponding diamond of superconformal algebras \cite{Fiset:2018huv, Fiset:2021ruv}.
elements.id-string-153: This serves the twofold purpose of establishing some notation that will be used throughout the rest of the note as well as presenting the construction of the TCS diamond as a warm-up case for the Schoen manifold.
elements.id-string-155: As discussed in \cref{sec:introConnSum}, the idea of the TCS construction is to glue two Asymptotically Cylindrical (ACyl) manifolds---called \emph{building blocks}---along their isomorphic asymptotic ends.
elements.id-string-156: This is done via a \emph{gluing map} that identifies the \emph{cross-sections} of the cylinders and produces a compact manifold $M$ with a long \emph{neck} region.
elements.id-string-157: This manifold has a well-defined G$_2$-structure that becomes torsion-free after a certain deformation.
elements.id-string-158: Firstly, we need to introduce the concept of Asymptotically Cylindrical (ACyl) Calabi--Yau $n$-fold (CY$_n$).
elements.id-string-159: This is an open Calabi--Yau $n$-fold which asymptotes a cylinder with cross-section given by a Calabi--Yau $(n-1)$-fold times a circle $\Sc^1$, that is
elements.id-string-161: Denoting by $(t,\theta)$ the coordinates of $\R^+\times \Sc^1$, the metric $g_n\,$, Hermitian form $\omega_n$ and holomorphic volume form $\Omega_n$ of the $\text{ACyl CY}_n$ satisfy the following asymptotic relations
elements.id-string-164: For a TCS manifold, each of the building blocks consist on an ACyl Calabi--Yau 3-fold times a circle, $M_\pm=\Sc^1_{\xi\pm}\times\text{ACyl CY}_{3\pm}\,$.
elements.id-string-165: We call these circles the \emph{external} circles and parametrize them by coordinates $\xi_\pm\,$.
elements.id-string-166: The cross-sections of these building blocks are given by $N_\pm=\text{CY}_{2\pm}\times\Sc^1_{\theta\pm}\times\Sc^1_{\xi\pm}$, where the circles $\Sc^1_{\theta\pm}$ coming from the $\text{CY}_{3\pm}$ are called \emph{internal} circles and we denote their coordinates by $\theta_\pm\,$.
elements.id-string-169: Each of the building blocks admits a G$_2$-structure that can be described in terms of an \emph{associative} 3-form.
elements.id-string-170: We denote these forms by $\varphi_\pm$ and define them in terms of the forms on the Calabi--Yau 3-folds and the external circles
elements.id-string-172: Parametrizing the $\R^+_\pm$ factors by coordinates $t_\pm \,$, these forms follow the asymptotic behaviour
elements.id-string-174: where we have made explicit the hyper-K\"ahler structure of the K3 surfaces $\text{CY}_{2\pm}$ identifying
elements.id-string-176: The gluing map $F$ between the two asymptotic ends identifies the external circle on $M_+$ with the internal circle on $M_-$ and vice-versa.
elements.id-string-177: In order to compensate this ``twist'', the K3 surfaces are identified via a \emph{hyper-K\"ahler matching}: this is an isometry of the K3 surfaces that effectively rotates the hyper-K\"ahler structures.
elements.id-string-178: At the level of differential forms, the effect of the gluing map $F$ is as follows
elements.id-string-179: \begin{equation}  F^*(\dd t_-)&=-\dd t_+\, ,& F^*(\dd\xi_-)&=\dd\theta_+\, ,& F^*(\dd\theta_-)&=\dd\xi_+\, ,  F^*(\omega^K_-)&=-\omega^K_+\, ,& F^*(\omega^I_-)&=\omega^J_+\, ,& F^*(\omega^J_-)&=\omega^I_+\, . \end{equation}
elements.id-string-180: Note the gluing map identifies the asymptotic ends of the associative 3-forms $\varphi_\pm$ \eqref{eq:coassociativeasymptotic} and provides a well-defined G$_2$-structure to the compact manifold $M$.

elements.id-string-183: We now summarize how the diamond of algebras corresponding to the TCS construction can be obtained, showing explicitly the inclusions of the most important generators.
elements.id-string-184: The guiding principle for the algebra inclusions are the asymptotic geometric relations we have just described.
elements.id-string-185: The algebra at the top of the diamond corresponds to the neck region, which has the form $\R^+\times\Sc^1\times\Sc^1\times\text{CY}_{2}\,$.
elements.id-string-186: This immediately implies that the associated algebra is $\text{Fr}^3\oplus \text{Od}_2\,$.
elements.id-string-187: The neck region can be described from the point of view of $R^+_+\times N_+$ or $R^+_-\times N_-$, to be completely explicit we follow the $R^+_+\times N_+$ description here.

elements.id-string-205: Superconformal algebras for the Schoen Calabi--Yau manifold
elements.id-string-206: In this section we provide new results regarding the diamond of worldsheet algebras associated to the Schoen manifold \cite{Schoen1988}.
elements.id-string-207: The Schoen manifold is a Calabi--Yau 3-fold with Hodge numbers $\left( h^{1,1}, h^{2,1} \right)=(19,19)$ and it has been extensively studied together with its quotients in the context of F-theory and heterotic compactifications, see for example \cite{Morrison:1996pp, Gopakumar:1996mu, Curio:1997rn, Braun:2005ux, Braun:2005nv, Candelas:2007ac, Apruzzi:2014dza}.
elements.id-string-208: The Schoen manifold is also known in the literature as the split bicubic because it can be realized via a complete intersection with configuration matrix
elements.id-string-210: We will not need a detailed understanding of the Schoen manifold as a CICY, but it will be useful to keep in mind that the Schoen manifold can be described as a fibration over $\mathbb{CP}^1$ whose generic fiber is given by two elliptic surfaces (i.e. two 2-tori).
elements.id-string-211: We are interested in the Schoen manifold as a connected sum.
elements.id-string-212: This was explicitly described in \cite{Braun:2017uku} using the duality between M-theory on a K3 surface and heterotic string theory on a 3-torus and we present a summary of the main ideas in \cref{sec:SchoenfromMtheory}.
elements.id-string-213: We also present a complementary description of the Schoen manifold as an orbifold resolution in \cref{sec:Schoenasorbifold}.
elements.id-string-214: We then move to a description of the worldsheet chiral algebras, introducing the corresponding diamond in \cref{sec:Schoendiamond} and discussing its genericity in \cref{sec:Schoengeneric}.
elements.id-string-215: We conclude in \cref{sec:Schoenautomorphisms} with a study of automorphisms of the diamond which include a realization of SYZ mirror symmetry in the worldsheet.
elements.id-string-216: The Schoen manifold as a connected sum
elements.id-string-217: We summarize the discussion of \cite{Braun:2017uku} leading to the connected sum decomposition of the Schoen manifold and refer the reader to the original paper for further details.
elements.id-string-218: The key idea is a fiberwise application of the duality between M-theory on a K3 surface and heterotic string theory on a 3-torus \cite{Acharya:1996ci, Acharya:2001gy, Gukov:2002jv}.
elements.id-string-219: Consider an M-theory compactification of a TCS G$_2$-manifold\footnote{We follow the notation introduced in \cref{sec:TCSgeometry}.} and focus on its building blocks, $M_\pm=\Sc^1_{\xi\pm}\times\text{ACyl CY}_{3\pm}\,$.
elements.id-string-220: The standard procedure to construct ACyl Calabi--Yau 3-folds \cite{Corti:2012, Corti:2012kd} is to start from a closed K\"ahler 3-fold given by a K3 fibration over $\mathbb{CP}^1$ (satisfying certain properties) and then remove a point from the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ as well as the K3 fiber over that point.
elements.id-string-221: We can thus think of each $\text{ACyl CY}_{3\pm}$ as a fibration: the fiber is a K3 surface $\text{CY}_{2\pm}$ and the base $B_\pm$ is given by $\mathbb{CP}^1$ minus a point.
elements.id-string-222: These fibrations realize the asymptotic cylindrical behaviour \eqref{eq:TCSasymptoticbuildingblock}, where $(t_\pm,\theta_\pm)$ are the asymptotic coordinates of $B_\pm\longrightarrow\R^+_\pm\times\Sc^1_{\theta\pm}\,$.
elements.id-string-223: For technical reasons, we assume that the $\text{CY}_{2\pm}$ fibers are themselves given by an elliptic fibration over $\mathbb{CP}^1$ with a well-defined section, and we further assume that the elliptic curves are holomorphically fibered over the $\mathbb{CP}^1$.
elements.id-string-224: These assumptions imply that when the $\text{CY}_{2\pm}$ are fibered over $B_\pm$ to give the $\text{ACyl CY}_{3\pm}\,$, the Hermitian forms $\omega_{2\pm}=\omega^I_{\pm}$ remain constant whereas the holomorphic volume forms $\Omega_{2\pm}=\omega^J_{\pm}+i\,\omega^K_{\pm}$ vary over the fibration.
elements.id-string-225: We can now consider the dual heterotic picture by applying M-theory/heterotic duality to the K3 fibers $\text{CY}_{2\pm}\,$.
elements.id-string-226: These are then replaced by 3-torus fibers $\mathbb{T}^3_\pm$ while keeping the base $B_\pm$ and the external circle $\Sc^1_{\xi\pm}$ intact.
elements.id-string-227: This duality establishes a relation between the circles $\Sc^1_{a\pm}$ of the $\mathbb{T}^3_\pm$ fibers and the Hermitian forms $\omega^a_\pm$ of the $\text{CY}_{2\pm}$ via a period decomposition, where $a\in\lbrace I,J,K\rbrace$.
elements.id-string-228: In particular, the $\mathbb{T}^3_\pm$ fiber factorizes as $\mathbb{T}_{f\pm}\times \Sc^1_{I\pm}$ in the following way: the $\Sc^1_{I\pm}$ circle---which is related to the Hermitian forms $\omega^I_{\pm}$ that remain constant in the $\text{CY}_{2\pm}$ fibers---is trivially fibered over $B_\pm\,$, whereas the torus $\mathbb{T}_{f\pm}=\Sc^1_{J\pm}\times\Sc^1_{K\pm}$ is non-trivially fibered over $B_\pm$ and gives rise to a new open Calabi--Yau 2-fold.
elements.id-string-229: Therefore, after M-theory/heterotic duality we obtain the dual building blocks $\widetilde{M}_\pm = \Sc^1_{\xi\pm}\times \Sc^1_{I\pm} \times \widetilde{\text{CY}}_{2\pm} \,$, where the $\widetilde{\text{CY}}_{2\pm}$ factors are given by the $\mathbb{T}_{f\pm}$ fibration over $B_\pm\,$.
elements.id-string-230: These building blocks are again asymptotically cylindrical with a cross-section given by a product of five circles:
elements.id-string-232: In what follows we denote by $(x_{I\pm},x_{J\pm},x_{K\pm})$ the coordinates on the circles $\Sc^1_{I\pm}\times\Sc^1_{J\pm}\times\Sc^1_{K\pm}\,$.
elements.id-string-233: Since the glued TCS manifold has G$_2$-holonomy, the duality implies that the compact manifold $\widetilde{M}$ obtained after gluing $\widetilde{M}_\pm$ will be a Calabi--Yau 3-fold.
elements.id-string-234: We therefore want to define an $\text{SU}(3)$-structure on each building block $\widetilde{M}_\pm\,$, this can be done mimicking the ACyl CY asymptotic relations \eqref{eq:hermitianasymptotic} and \eqref{eq:holomorphicasymptotic}
elements.id-string-236: where $(\widetilde{\omega}_{2\pm} , \widetilde{\Omega}_{2\pm} )$ are the Hermitian and holomorphic volume forms on the $\widetilde{\text{CY}}_{2\pm}\,$.
elements.id-string-237: Their correct asymptotic behaviour is again provided by the duality, for example $\widetilde{\omega}_{2\pm,\infty}$ can be read off directly from \eqref{eq:coassociativeasymptotic} following the identification between Hermitian forms and circles,
elements.id-string-238: \begin{equation}  \widetilde{\omega}_{2\pm} & \longrightarrow \widetilde{\omega}_{2\pm,\infty}=\dd\theta_\pm\wedge\dd x_{J\pm}+\dd t_\pm\wedge\dd x_{K\pm} \, ,  \widetilde{\Omega}_{2\pm} & \longrightarrow \widetilde{\Omega}_{2\pm,\infty}=(\dd  x_{J\pm}-i\dd\theta_\pm)\wedge(\dd x_{K\pm}-i\dd t_\pm) \, . \end{equation}
elements.id-string-239: Combining \eqref{eq:CY2hermitianasymptotic} and \eqref{eq:CY2holomorphicasymptotic} with \eqref{eq:SchoenSU3} we find the asymptotic behaviour of the $\text{SU}(3)$-structure with respect to the neck region
elements.id-string-240: \begin{equation}  \widetilde{\omega}_{3\pm} & \longrightarrow \widetilde{\omega}_{3\pm,\infty}=\dd\xi_\pm\wedge\dd x_{I\pm} +\dd\theta_\pm\wedge\dd x_{J\pm}+\dd t_\pm\wedge\dd x_{K\pm} \, ,  \widetilde{\Omega}_{3\pm} & \longrightarrow \widetilde{\Omega}_{3\pm,\infty}=(\dd x_{I\pm}-i\dd\xi_\pm)\wedge(\dd  x_{J\pm}-i\dd\theta_\pm)\wedge(\dd x_{K\pm}-i\dd t_\pm) \, . \end{equation}

elements.id-string-242: It remains to identify the gluing map $\widetilde{F}$ that can be used to fuse $\widetilde{M}_\pm$ together to obtain the compact dual manifold $\widetilde{M}$.

elements.id-string-254: They find $\left( h^{1,1}, h^{2,1} \right)=(19,19)$, which uniquely identifies the connected sum Calabi--Yau 3-fold to be the Schoen manifold.
elements.id-string-255: An important observation is that all M-theory compactifications on TCS G$_2$-manifolds with the technical assumptions we have considered---such as having elliptically fibered K3 fibers---are dual to heterotic compactifications on the same Calabi--Yau manifold.
